frames.narration: An analyst types SELECT A, COUNT(B) FROM T GROUP BY A over a table with a trillion nested records. There is no load step: the table is already in GFS, stored column by column.

messages.label: SELECT A, COUNT(B) FROM T GROUP BY A

frames.narration: The root server works out which tablets, the horizontal pieces of the table, make up T, and rewrites the query for the next level: each child gets a COUNT over its share of the tablets, and the root will SUM the counts.

messages.label: COUNT over your share of the tablets

frames.narration: The intermediate servers pass smaller shares down to the leaf servers. A slot is one thread on a leaf, and the table has many more tablets than slots, so each slot handles several tablets, a few at a time.

Each leaf reads only the column stripes the query mentions, A and B, and not the other hundreds of fields. The stripes carry repetition and definition levels, so the leaf can count values within records without ever assembling a record.

messages.label: read stripes A and B only

frames.narration: One tablet is on a slow machine. The dispatcher keeps a histogram of tablet processing times and sees that this one is far above the rest. It reschedules the tablet on another server, which reads a different one of its three replicas.
Partial counts flow up the tree. Each intermediate server adds up the counts from its leaves, and the root adds up the intermediate servers' results. Small and medium results suit this well.

The root returns the answer. If the analyst had asked for results once 98% of the tablets were scanned, it could have answered sooner, without waiting for the slowest few. A query that took a MapReduce job minutes to hours returns in seconds.
